blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Audio descriptions (AD) are essential for making visual media accessible to blind and low-vision (BLV) users. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a scalable solution for generating audio descriptions on-demand, their performance on ``inline'' audio descriptions -- which must fit within existing silences in a video -- remains under-explored, particularly for diverse user-generated content (UGC). We present a comprehensive investigation into MLLM-generated inline audio descriptions. First, we introduce MTG-AD, a professionally annotated dataset of 36 hours of videos, each averaging $\sim$5 mins. and 8k+ descriptions in total, co-created by paired blind and sighted AD professionals to provide a high-quality benchmark for this task. Second, we propose MTG-AD-Eval, an evaluation framework based on audio description expert guidelines that provides fine-grained, reference-free actionable metrics for model improvement. Crucially, our framework evaluates the end-to-end task: it renders the generated scripts into audio tracks to assess their fit within the original video's natural silences, minimizing disruptive overlaps. Our analysis across frontier MLLMs reveals that while models accurately describe visual events and substantially reduce speech overlaps, gaps persist in narrative pacing and flow. Finally, we empirically validate that our automated and reference-free metrics correlate significantly with human quality ratings from sighted raters and 7 BLV participants, finding that while users narrowly prefer human-authored audio descriptions, they find MLLM-generated audio descriptions highly beneficial for comprehension. We provide actionable system design guidance and release MTG-AD at https://hf.co/datasets/google/mind-the-gap-inline-ad and MTG-AD-Eval at https://github.com/google/mtg-ad.
blocks.zh: 音频描述(AD)对于盲人和低视(BLV)用户无障碍使用视觉媒体至关重要. 虽然多式联运大语言模型(MLLMs)为按需生成音频描述提供了一个可扩展的解决方案,但其在“inline”音频描述上的性能 -- -- 必须与视频中的现有沉默一致 -- -- 仍然没有得到充分利用,特别是对于用户生成的多种内容(UGC)而言。 我们对MLLM产生的内含音频描述进行全面调查。 首先,我们介绍MTG-AD,一个由36小时视频组成的专业附加说明的数据集,每集平均5分。 和8k+的描述,由双盲和有视力的AD专业人员共同创建,为这项任务提供高质量的基准. 第二,我们提出MTG-AD-Eval,这是一个基于音频描述专家准则的评价框架,为模型改进提供了精细、无参考可操作的衡量标准。 关键是,我们的框架评价了端到端的任务:它使生成的脚本被收录入音频轨道,以评估它们是否适合原视频的自然沉默,将破坏性重叠降到最低. 我们跨越前沿的MLLMs的分析表明,虽然模型准确地描述了视觉事件并大大减少了语音重叠,但在叙事速度和流量方面仍然存在差距. 最后,我们通过经验验证,我们的自动化和无参考度的衡量标准与视觉测评人和7名BLV参与者的人类质量评级密切相关,发现虽然用户狭隘地倾向于人类授权的音频描述,但他们认为MLLM生成的音频描述非常有利于理解。 我们在https://hf.co/datasets/google/mind-the-gap-inline-ad和MTG-AD-Eval上提供可操作的系统设计指导并发布MTG-AD。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Blind and low-vision (BLV) viewers turn to user-generated videos to learn new skills, pursue hobbies, and stay informed [ 17 ] . Yet creators rarely verbalize essential visual details, leaving many videos hard to follow [ 17 , 18 ] . Audio descriptions (AD) make videos accessible by narrating key visual events to complement the existing audio [ 1 , 31 ] . Unlike extended AD that pauses playback, inline AD preserves the video’s runtime by fitting descriptions into natural pauses ( Fig. 1 ). Effective inline AD thus goes beyond listing what is on screen: it requires temporal precision and content selectivity to build a coherent narrative that enriches, rather than repeats or interrupts, the original audio.
blocks.zh: 盲视和低视(BLV)观众转向用户制作的视频学习新技能,追求爱好,保持知情[17]. 但创作者很少对基本的视觉细节说出话, 音频描述(AD)通过叙述关键视觉事件来获取视频,以补充现有的音频[1,31]. 与暂停播放的扩展AD不同,内置AD通过将描述配对到自然暂停来保存视频的运行时间(图1). 因此,有效的内含AD超越了列出屏幕上的内容:它需要时间精确度和内容选择性来构建一个连贯的叙述,丰富而不是重复或中断原始音频.

blocks.en: While high-quality audio descriptions are professionally crafted for film and TV [ 22 ] , it is rarely available for user-generated videos [ 17 ] , motivating semi-automated [ 18 , 24 , 36 , 5 ] and automated generation approaches [ 32 , 16 , 3 , 34 , 8 , 15 ] that have the potential to scale access for millions of BLV audience members.
blocks.zh: 虽然高质量的音频描述是为电影和电视制作的[22],但很少提供给用户制作的视频[17],激发半自动[18、24、36、5]和自动化生成方法[32、16、3、34、8、15],这些方法有可能扩大数百万BLV观众的获取范围。

blocks.en:
Figure 1 : Temporal Constraints of Inline Audio Descriptions. Inline AD must fit precisely into natural silences within a video’s narration (purple).
Both the professional “Gold” human AD from MTG-AD (green) and our model-generated “AutoAD” (orange) fit within these tight temporal gaps without overlapping speech. While AutoAD generates vivid, coherent descriptions with timing-aware prompts, the professional AD achieves stronger narrative flow by capturing camera perspectives ( e.g. , “drone footage”).
blocks.zh:
图1:内含音频描述的时间限制。 内线AD必须精确地融入视频描述(纯度)中的自然沉默。
来自MTG-AD(绿色)的专业“黄金”人类AD和我们模型产生的“AutoAD”(橙色)都符合这些紧凑的时间差距,没有重叠的言论。 虽然AutoAD生成生动,连贯的描述,带有时间意识的提示,但专业AD通过捕捉镜头视角(如"drone footes")实现更强的叙事流.

blocks.en: Recent progress in general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) makes it newly possible to generate AD scripts directly from video. Models such as Gemini 2.5/3.5 [ 7 ] , GPT-5.2 [ 21 ] , and Qwen-3.5-Omni [ 25 ] can take a video as input and output a timestamped narration script to be rendered via text-to-speech (TTS). Yet are MLLM-generated audio descriptions understandable and enjoyable for BLV audiences of user-generated videos? Answering this requires evaluating the full end-to-end pipeline: generating the AD script, synthesizing speech via TTS, and measuring how well the rendered audio fits within the natural silences of the original video.
blocks.zh: 通用多式联运大语言模型(MLLMs)的近期进展使得从视频直接生成AD脚本成为新可能. 双子座2.5/3.5 [7],GPT-5.2 [21],以及Quen-3.5-Omni [25] 等型号可以将一段视频作为输入,输出一个时间标注的解说脚本,通过文本对语音(TTS)进行渲染. 然而,MLLM生成的音频描述对BLV用户生成的视频的观众来说是可以理解的和可以享受的吗? 回答这一点需要评价整个端到端的管道:生成AD脚本,通过TTS合成语音,以及测量所制作的音频在原视频的自然静默中是否适合.

blocks.en: Prior work largely evaluates generated AD on trimmed video segments against a single reference [ 9 , 35 ] , through short-clip human ratings, or with coarse LLM scores [ 15 ] . Evaluating isolated clips out of context misses sequence-level coherence [ 14 ] , spoken AD duration, un-narrated “dead air” gaps, and speech overlaps that shape the end-to-end BLV listening experience. Moreover, unlike movies with professional reference AD [ 27 ] , user-generated videos rarely have expert annotations, forcing prior benchmarks to rely on synthetic [ 9 ] or novice-authored proxies where coarse metrics quickly saturate [ 15 ] .
blocks.zh: 先前的工作主要通过人类短片的收视率或粗糙的LLM分数,根据单一参考[9,35],对剪辑视频段生成的AD进行评审[15]. 从上下文来评价孤立的片段,错过了序列级的一致性[14],口语AD持续时间,未描述的"死气沉沉"缺口,以及影响端到端的BLV监听经验的语音重叠. 此外,与具有专业参考AD[27]的电影不同,用户制作的视频很少有专家说明,迫使先前的基准依赖人工合成[9]或新作者代词,粗度度度量迅速饱和[15].

blocks.en: Our work makes three contributions: First, we establish a high-quality benchmark for inline AD on user-generated videos , MTG-AD, comprising professionally crafted ADs for 433 YouTube videos ( ∼ 36 {\sim}36 hours) co-created by paired blind and sighted AD specialists, alongside outputs from nine frontier MLLMs. Second, we introduce MTG-AD-Eval, an end-to-end, reference-free evaluation framework grounded in expert AD guidelines that pairs TTS-based temporal metrics with multimodal LLM judges, analyzing cross-judge biases and transfer to YouDescribe. Finally, we validate our metrics and benchmark against human judgments from sighted raters and 7 BLV participants, showing strong alignment with human ratings, including resolving reference-matching constraints in prior works, and identifying where frontier MLLMs still trail human narrative pacing.
blocks.zh: 我们的工作有三项贡献: 首先,我们为用户制作的视频(MTG-AD)设定了高质量的AD内置基准,其中包括专业设计的AD,用于433个YouTube视频( 36 {\sim}36小时),由配对的盲人和视障的AD专家共同制作,以及9个前沿MLLM的产品。 第二,我们引入了MTG-AD-Eval,这是一种基于专家反倾销准则的终到无参考评价框架,该准则将基于TTS的时间度量衡与多式联运LM法官结合,分析跨法官的偏差,并转让给YouDescription。 最后,我们验证了我们的衡量尺度和基准,以比照视觉测评员和7名BLV参与者对人类的判断,显示与人类评级的高度一致,包括解决以往作品的参照比对限制,并查明边疆的MLLM仍然追随人类叙事速度。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Table 1 : Comparison of Audio Description Datasets. Prior movie and TV benchmarks evaluate isolated silent intervals using pre-trimmed clips or pre-extracted visual features, while prior user-generated or instructional datasets rely on volunteer narrations, short clips with ignored audio, or synthetic ASR adaptations. MTG-AD provides full-length user-generated videos co-annotated by paired sighted and blind AD professionals and evaluates end-to-end inline AD across each entire video.
blocks.zh: 表1:音频描述数据集比较. 先前的电影和电视基准使用预刻片段或预提取的视觉功能来评价孤立的无声间隔,而之前的用户生成或指令数据集则依赖于志愿者的叙述,短片段带有被忽视的音频,或合成ASR的改编. MTG-AD提供全长用户制作的视频,由配对的视力和盲目AD专业人士共同附加说明,并评价每段视频的端到端内置AD.

blocks.en: Audio Description Datasets. Most existing AD benchmarks draw from professional descriptions created for movies [ 27 , 29 , 8 , 35 , 9 ] or TV series [ 34 ] ( Tab. 1 ). While these corpora establish what and how to describe in scripted entertainment, user-generated videos vary widely in intent, camera work, editing pace, on-screen text, and speech density, from silent montages to near-continuous narration. Movie AD benchmarks also evaluate models on pre-trimmed 2–20 s clips around known AD timestamps, whereas inline AD for user-generated content requires reasoning over untrimmed, multi-minute videos (averaging 5 minutes in MTG-AD, a horizon shared with long-video benchmarks such as Neptune [ 19 ] ) to decide both when and what to describe. Because professional AD rarely exists for user-generated videos, prior datasets rely on volunteer descriptions of uneven quality on YouDescribe [ 28 ] , synthetic MLLM descriptions of short ∼ 10 {\sim}10 s clips [ 15 ] , or repurposed narrations from instructional videos [ 9 ] . MTG-AD addresses this gap with 36 hours of full-length user-generated videos co-annotated by paired sighted and blind AD professionals.
blocks.zh: 音频描述数据集. 现有的反倾销基准大多来自为电影[27、29、8、35、9]或电视连续剧[34]创造的专业描述(附件1)。 虽然这些corpora确定了在剧本娱乐中什么和如何描述,但用户制作的视频在意图,相机工作,编辑速度,屏幕上文本,以及语音密度等方面差异很大,从沉默的蒙太奇到近乎连续的叙述. Movie AD基准还围绕已知的AD时间戳来评价预切2–20 s片段的模型,而用户生成内容的内置AD则需要对未切入的多分钟视频进行推理(在MTG-AD中录制5分钟,与海王星等长视频基准共享的视野[19]),以决定何时和如何描述。 因为专业的AD很少为用户制作的视频存在,所以之前的数据集依赖于YouDescription上对质量不均匀的志愿者描述[28],合成的MLLM描述短篇的QQ 10 ~sim}10 scripts [15],或者从教学视频中重新命名的叙述[9]. MTG-AD用36小时的全长用户制作的视频来弥补这一差距,这些视频由双目和盲目的AD专业人员共同注释。

MTG-AD comprises 433 professionally annotated videos ( ∼ 36 {\sim}36 hours): (a) video durations center around 5 minutes; (b) human-annotated AD segments per minute; (c) vlogs form the largest category alongside travel, nature, and education; both (d) speech density and (e) silence-gap distribution illustrate the tight pauses into which inline AD must fit.

blocks.en: Evaluating Audio Descriptions. Automated AD evaluation largely compares generated text against a ground-truth reference [ 6 ] , using n-gram or embedding similarity metrics such as BLEU [ 23 ] and BERTScore [ 37 ] , or domain-specific metrics for character naming and semantic alignment such as MNScore [ 35 ] , CRITIC [ 9 ] , and LLM-AD-Eval [ 9 ] . However, single-reference similarity on isolated clips poorly reflects listener comprehension and penalizes valid alternative descriptions. Recent work moves beyond isolated single-reference scoring toward sequence-level coherence [ 14 ] and QA-based comprehension checks [ 13 ] , yet still evaluates text scripts without rendering audio to test whether descriptions fit natural pauses without overlapping speech or leaving long silences.
blocks.zh: 评估音频描述。 自动反倾销评价在很大程度上比较了生成的文本与地面真实参照[6],使用正方克或嵌入类似度量,如BLEU[23]和BERTScore[37],或用于字符命名和语义对齐的域特定度量,如MNScore[35]、CRITIC[9]和LLM-AD-Eval[9]。 然而,孤立片段的单引用相似性不能很好地反映听众的理解并惩罚有效的替代描述. 最近的工作超越了孤立的单引用评分,走向序列级一致性[14]和基于QA的理解检查[13],但仍在不提供音频的情况下评价文本脚本,以测试描述是否适合自然暂停而不重叠的言论或留下长时间的沉默.

blocks.en: Human studies with external raters or BLV listeners better capture end-to-end playback quality, though full-video listening studies are time-consuming and typically cover few videos [ 2 , 24 ] . On short ∼ 10 {\sim}10 s clips, VideoA11y [ 15 ] found that guideline-prompted MLLM descriptions surpassed novice captions and matched trained describers, and that LLM-as-a-judge ratings aligned with BLV judgments, echoing broader findings on LLM judges for audio captioning [ 33 ] . Still, prior work has not evaluated end-to-end inline AD on full-length user-generated videos, compared MLLM outputs against professionally co-authored AD in that setting, or validated reference-free timing and quality metrics against sighted and BLV listeners.
blocks.zh: 带有外部评分器或BLV收听器的人类研究更好地捕捉到端到端的回放质量,尽管全视频监听研究很耗时,通常覆盖很少的视频[2,24]. VideoA11y [15] 在短篇的 \\ 10\ sim}10 s 剪辑上发现,由准则制成的 MLLM 描述超越了新标题,并配对了训练有素的描述者, LLM as-a-judge 评分与 BLV 判决一致,与 LLM 评分上更广泛的结论相呼应,用于音频标题 [33]. 然而,以前的工作还没有在用户制作的全长视频上评价端到端的内置AD,没有将MLLM产出与专业合著的AD进行比较,也没有对视线和BLV听众进行验证无参考时间和质量衡量。

blocks.en: 3 Mind the Gap (MTG-AD) Dataset
blocks.zh: 3 注意差距(MTG-AD)数据集

blocks.en: MTG-AD benchmarks end-to-end inline audio description on user-generated YouTube videos, a domain frequently watched by BLV viewers [ 17 , 28 , 15 ] where professional AD rarely exists ( Figs. 1 and 2 ). The dataset comprises 433 English videos ( ∼ 35.9 {\sim}35.9 hours; mean 5.0 5.0 min) partitioned into 332 validation videos for prompt and method development and 101 test videos for multi-model evaluation. Each video includes inline AD co-authored by paired sighted and blind AD professionals, a timestamped YouTube ASR transcript ( 26.3 % 26.3\% of videos have no transcribed speech, such as music-backed montages), and pre-extracted dense visual event lists ( 𝒟 \mathcal{D} , Sec. 4 ). For the 101 test videos, we also release unedited AD scripts and per-video metric scores across 12 model–prompt configurations spanning four prompting strategies and nine frontier multimodal models.
blocks.zh: MTG-AD 基准 用户生成的内置音频描述 YouTube视频,BLV观众经常观看的一个领域[17,28,15],专业AD很少存在(图1和图2. 数据集包括433个英语视频(35.9 {\sim}35.9小时;平均5.0 5.0分钟),被分割成332个验证视频,用于快速和方法开发,101个测试视频用于多模式评价. 每个视频包括由配对的视力和盲目的AD专业人士共同制作的内线AD,一个时间标注的YouTube ASR记录稿(26.3% 26.3%的视频没有转录的语音,如音乐支持的蒙塔吉斯),以及预摘录的密集视觉事件列表(D\mathcal{D}, Sec.4 ). 对于101个测试视频,我们也发布未经编辑的AD脚本和每集视频的评分,覆盖12个模型的即时配置,跨越4个促动策略和9个前沿多式联运模式。

blocks.en: 3.1 Video Selection and Filtering
blocks.zh: 3.1 视频选择和过滤

blocks.en:
We sampled 557 candidate English videos around 3–7 minutes long from YouTube channels with at least 1,000 subscribers across diverse user-generated categories, led by vlogs (46%), education (16%), cooking, nature, travel, and science in the final set ( Fig. 2 c). The professional AD teams reviewed every candidate in full to assess whether inline AD could be added without pausing playback, filtering candidates on two criteria:
(i) Temporal viability : videos with nonstop dialogue or narration, or vlogs whose on-screen subtitles left no audio space for additional descriptions, were marked non-viable, though annotators revisited borderline cases to include partial descriptions where brief pauses permitted; and
(ii) Topical diversity : after annotating 3–5 videos of a recurring style ( e.g. , overhead cooking tutorials), further near-duplicates were skipped.
Of the 557 candidates, 438 ( 78.6 % 78.6\% ) were annotated, 92 ( 16.5 % 16.5\% ) were excluded as non-viable, and 27 ( 4.8 % 4.8\% ) were skipped for redundancy. Five duplicate candidates were annotated twice; retaining the first annotation yields 433 unique videos totaling 35.9 35.9 hours ( Fig. 2 a,d).
blocks.zh:
我们从YouTube频道抽取了大约3-7分钟左右的557个候选英语视频,其中至少1 000个用户来自不同的用户类别,由Vlogs(46%)、教育(16%)、烹饪、自然、旅行和科学(图2c)领头。 专业反倾销小组全面审查了每个候选人,以评估是否可以在不浪费回放的情况下添加内在反倾销,根据两个标准筛选候选人:
(一) 临时可行性:屏幕字幕没有录音空间供补充说明的视频或无间歇对话或叙述的Vlog被标记为不可行,尽管注释者重新审视了边缘情况,以便在允许短暂暂停的情况下列入部分描述;
(二) 专题多样性:在对重复播放的3至5个录像(例如,上层烹饪辅导)进行注释后,又省略了几近重复的录像。
在557名候选人中,438名(78.6%为78.6)被注解,92名(16.5%为16.5%为16.5)被排除,27名(4.8%为4.8%为4.8%)因冗余而被跳过。 5个重复的候选者被两次注解;保留了第1个注释的433个独有录像,共计35.9个35.9小时(图2 a,d)。

blocks.en: 3.2 Professionally Co-Authored AD
blocks.zh: 3.2 专业联合认证的反倾销

blocks.en: Descriptions were produced by two two-person professional teams, each pairing one sighted and one blind AD writer so that every script reflects both visual detail and BLV listener priorities. For each video, the sighted writer first watched the full video to establish narrative context and pacing, then rewatched it in segments to draft concise, timestamped descriptions of key visual events and on-screen text not already conveyed by speech or sound effects. Next, the writer imported the script into an audio-editing environment against the original soundtrack, adjusting phrasing and start times so each spoken description fit cleanly into natural pauses without overlapping dialogue. Finally, the blind writing partner reviewed the timed playback end-to-end to audit narrative clarity and standalone comprehension before sign-off. Across all 433 videos, MTG-AD contains 8,126 AD segments (6,214 validation, 1,912 test), with a mean of 18.8 (median 16, IQR 10–26) segments per video, 17.0 words per segment (median 15), and a median rate of 3.4 segments per minute (IQR 2.0–5.7; Fig. 2 b).

blocks.en:
Unlike trimmed-clip captioning with pre-segmented gaps, generating inline AD on untrimmed videos requires a model to select salient visual events while aligning to speech pauses and fitting spoken AD within each gap.
To study how well MLLMs handle this end-to-end task and what context or reasoning steps resolve their failure modes, we designed four prompts that we studied on Gemini-2.5 Flash. Simple AD ( Fig. 17 ) tests minimal-instruction capability, requesting only timestamped descriptions during non-speech intervals; Guideline only ( Fig. 18 ) adds expert AD rules ( e.g. , prioritizing key visuals, reading on-screen text verbatim, remaining objective, and omitting audible cues), testing whether domain guidelines suffice when speech pauses must be inferred directly from video; Guideline + ASR ( Fig. 19 ) supplies the timestamped speech transcript (start and end times) and a 1 1 – 3 3 words/s speaking-rate target to ground pause boundaries in text; and Gd. + Timing ASR ( Fig. 20 ) decomposes temporal planning into explicit steps: computing each silent gap’s duration, capping length at 3 3 words per silent second (at most three sentences), and skipping details when space is insufficient.
To compare model families under our strongest elicitation setup ( Gd. + Timing ASR ), on the 101 test videos we pair all four Gemini-2.5 Flash prompt runs with eight additional frontier models: GPT-4.1 mini, GPT-5.2, Claude 4, Claude 4.5, Qwen-2-VL-Max, Gemini-3.5 Flash, and Qwen-3.5-Omni-Flash/Plus. Providing the timestamped transcript alongside the video gives both native audio-video models (Gemini-2.5/3.5 Flash, Qwen-3.5-Omni) and vision-and-text models identical speech content and silence boundaries without requiring raw audio ingestion.

blocks.en: From expert guidelines to metrics. Following prior work [ 24 , 15 ] , we reviewed five expert AD guidelines chosen for breadth and comprehensiveness: the American Council of the Blind [ 1 ] , DCMP’s Description Key [ 4 ] , ADLab’s film guide [ 26 ] , W3C’s WCAG [ 30 ] , and YouDescribe’s tips [ 28 ] . We also reviewed studies of BLV audiences’ perceptions of AD to find where audience preferences depart from prescribed rules [ 20 , 17 , 12 , 11 ] . Together with researchers in HCI, accessibility, and computer vision, we distilled these to ten guidelines covering content (G1–G4), style (G5–G6), and audio (G7–G10); Appx. A lists them all. In a pilot study, BLV audience members reviewed AD generated with a basic prompt and named the problems that most hurt their experience: AD talking over speech, long unexplained silences, and descriptions out-of-sync. We therefore turn the six guidelines tied to these problems (G1.1–G1.3, G2, G7, G8) into automatic metrics, and add the VideoA11y rubrics [ 15 ] to rate writing quality. Tab. 2 summarizes the metrics.

Timeliness (G2) measures how far each description is from the moment its event appears. A judge pairs each AD segment’s start time s i s_{i} with the event in 𝒟 \mathcal{D} it describes, occurring at time t i t_{i} , or marks it unmatched ( Fig. 24 ). Over the set M M of matched segments, we report Timeliness in seconds (unmatched segments are penalized by G1.1).
While Timeliness evaluates when AD starts, fitting inline AD into pauses depends on the rendered speech interval I i I_{i} so it shouldn’t spill into the next dialogue. Audio Overlaps (G7) is the total time during which AD and speech play together, T overlap = | A ∩ S | T_{\text{overlap}}=|A\cap S| . blocks.en: 4.3 Holistic Script Quality

blocks.en: Following VideoA11y [ 15 ] , an LLM judge rates the full AD script on a likert scale (1–5) on four dimensions: Descriptive (vivid, relevant visual detail), Objective (reports what is visible without speculation), Accurate (visual details are correct), and Clear (easy to follow without seeing the video). We evaluate two variants: • VideoA11y-Ref ( Fig. 25 ) is the original reference-based setup: the judge compares the generated AD with the human-written AD. A 5-minute video admits many valid descriptions, so its Accurate score effectively measures Reference Alignment , which penalizes correct details that the human describer happened not to mention. Human AD scored this way is compared with itself and therefore serves only as an upper bound. • Quality-RF (ours, Fig. 26 ) removes the reference human AD. The judge is given both the raw video (frames and audio) and the ASR transcript to ground spoken dialogue explicitly (input ablations in Appx. E ); it summarizes the video, explains its reasoning, and then scores the same four dimensions. This avoids the reference-matching penalty and works without human AD.

blocks.zh: 质量-RF(ours, fig. 26)删除参考的人类AD. 法官既获得原始录像(框架和音频),又获得ASR记录,以便明确进行地面口语对话(在Appx.E中输入伤痕);它总结录像,解释其推理,然后评分相同的四个维度。 这避免了参照比对处罚,并且在没有人类AD的情况下起作用.

blocks.en: Metric-guided prompt refinement. Scoring the four Gemini-2.5 Flash prompts across validation videos ( Fig. 3 , Tab. 4 ) illustrates how MTG-AD-Eval diagnoses failure modes to guide prompt design. Simple AD under-describes the video (Coverage 0.41 0.41 , Avg. Silence 17.95 17.95 s, On-Screen Text 0.47 0.47 ). Adding domain rules in Guideline only raises Prioritization ( 0.79 0.79 ) and On-Screen Text ( 0.69 0.69 ), yet MTG-AD-Eval exposes severe over-generation ( 1.23 1.23 Coverage, 59.19 59.19 s of speech overlap) that content metrics alone would miss. With Guideline + ASR which includes explicit time spans of dialogue overlaps reduce to 21.34 21.34 s. Further emphasizing per-gap duration and word-budget constraints in Gd. + Timing ASR reduces overlaps considerably to 12.77 12.77 s while preserving Prioritization ( 0.76 0.76 ). Human AD remains better timed ( 7.51 7.51 s overlap, 4.19 4.19 s Avg. Silence); its slightly lower Prioritization ( 0.73 0.73 ) arises because 𝒟 \mathcal{D} itself is MLLM-extracted, leaving fine-grained human-observed actions ( e.g. , a truck braking or swerving in Fig. 15 ) and brief pause-fitted beats (e.g. A seal blinking) uncredited.

Frontier models. We score nine models on the 101 test videos ( Fig. 4 , Tabs. 5 and 6 ).

Models scored with the Gemini-2.5 Flash judge ( Fig. 5 ) average 2.0 2.0 – 3.3 3.3 on Descriptive, Objective, and Clear ( 2.2 2.2 – 3.3 3.3 ) yet only 1.16 1.16 – 1.63 1.63 on Reference Alignment ( Accurate ). blocks.en: 5.2 LLM as Judge and Generalization
blocks.zh: 5.2 LLM 担任法官和通用

blocks.en: Inter-judge reliability. As observed with judgments of script quality between Gemini 2.5 Flash and 3.5 Flash judges, unconstrained Likert scores shift with judge leniency, so some changes and jumps conflates generator gains with the judge change. To test sensitivity to the evaluator, we re-score the same ADs with Claude, Gemini, GPT and Qwen judges and correlate their per-video scores on five LLM-judged metrics ( Fig. 6 a) All judge pairs correlate positively ( r = 0.38 r=0.38 – 0.74 0.74 ), and GPT-4.1 mini and Qwen-2-VL-Max agree most. However, calibration differs across judges ( Fig. 6 b): some judges are systematically more lenient ( e.g. , GPT-4.1 mini) and others harsher ( e.g. , Gemini-2.5-Flash), but these offsets are small. This supports using MLLM judges to rank systems, provided all systems in a comparison use the same judge.
blocks.zh: 法官之间的可靠性。 正如双子座2.5 Flash和3.5 Flash法官之间对脚本质量的判断所观察到的,不受约束的Irkrt分数随法官宽大处理而转移,因此一些变化和跳跃将生成器增益与法官的改变混为一谈. 为了测试对评价者的敏感性,我们与克劳德、双子座、GPT和Quen评委重新评分,并在五个LLM评分(图6(a))上将其按视频分数挂钩,所有评委对数正比(r=0.38 r=0.38=0.74 0.74),GPT-4.1小数和Qun-2-VL-Max最同意。 然而,各法官的校准不同(图6b):有些法官系统上比较宽大(如GPT-4.1小型),而另一些法官则比较苛刻(如双子座2.5-Flash),但这些抵消很小. 这支持使用劳动、劳动、劳工和土地管理法官进行等级制度,条件是所有系统在比较时都使用同一法官。

blocks.en: Generalization to YouDescribe. When applying our evaluation suite to external YouDescribe videos ( Fig. 7 ), we observe that “Premium” human AD trends ahead of “Standard” volunteer AD on Timeliness ( 2.16 2.16 s vs. 2.85 2.85 s) and Prioritization ( 0.82 0.82 vs. 0.80 0.80 ), though CIs overlap. This suggests that the metrics transfer to other user-generated videos and AD sources.

blocks.en: 5.3 Sighted and BLV Participant Studies & Metric Validation
blocks.zh: 5.3 研究与计量

blocks.en: We conducted complementary human studies with sighted raters and BLV participants using a custom playback interface. Sighted raters and BLV listeners serve distinct, complementary roles in evaluating AD [ 10 ] : sighted raters can directly inspect the video frames to verify visual-to-text faithfulness, missing visual events, and exact visual-timestamp alignment across many model/prompt pairs, whereas BLV participants evaluate whether the audio track and descriptions form a coherent, non-intrusive, and engaging standalone narrative without visual context.
blocks.zh: 我们利用自定义的回放界面,与视力检测员和BLV参与者进行了人类补充研究。 视觉测评员和BLV听众在评价AD[10]中起到不同,互补的作用:视觉测评员可以直接检查视频帧,以验证视觉对文字的忠实,缺失的视觉事件,以及许多模型/瞬间对子之间准确的视觉时间标配,而BLV参与者则评价音频轨迹和描述是否构成连贯,非侵扰性,在没有视觉背景的情况下参与独立叙述.

blocks.en: Sighted Rater Study. A pool of 8 sighted raters evaluated 42 videos, with AD instances spanning multiple models, prompts, and professional Human AD, across 11 dimensions including Coverage , Accuracy , Relevance , Clarity , Timeliness , and Audio Issues on a likert scale (full questionnaire in Appx. F ; and ratings of prompt comparison are in Fig. 10 ). Inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff’s α \alpha , Tab. 7 ) across all metrics was 0.654 0.654 , led by Timeliness ( 0.721 0.721 ) and Audio Issues ( 0.700 0.700 ). Comparing models ( Fig. 8 ), Gemini-2.5 Flash with Gd. + Timing ASR prompt approaches human ground truth in Accuracy and Timeliness but lags on audio overlap issues.

BLV Participant Study. We recruited 7 BLV participants who regularly watch YouTube. Each participant evaluated four videos randomly sampled from our dataset ( n = 28 n=28 video-level evaluations), listening to both AutoAD (Gemini-2.5 Flash with Gd. + Timing ASR ) and the professionally authored Human AD. Participants were unaware of the AD source and we randomized and counterbalanced the order of the AD sources. Participants provided ratings for each AD (Fig. 9 ), their preference between the two AD (Appx. Fig. 12 ), and qualitative feedback about each AD.
Participants rated both versions consistently high across all dimensions ( Fig. 9 ). While participants marginally preferred human-authored AD ( 53.6 % 53.6\% , Fig. 12 ), Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests showed statistically significant differences only for overall Satisfaction ( p < 0.05 p<0.05 ) and perceived Accuracy ( p < 0.05 p<0.05 ), with near-parity on Quality, Clarity, and Objectivity. Individual preferences varied markedly across content genres ( Sec. D.1 ): several participants preferred the denser visual detail of AutoAD for action- or travel-oriented clips while favoring the concise narrative pacing of professional human AD for dialogue-heavy vlogs.

blocks.en: Do the automated metrics agree with people? We compute video-level Spearman rank correlations between each metric and the matching human rating for both cohorts ( Tab. 3 ; full results in Appx. E ). For sighted raters, each data point is a rated video with its AD. For BLV listeners, each data point is one participant’s rating of the AutoAD version of a video ( n = 28 n=28 ), paired with that AD’s metric scores. Negative ρ \rho is expected for metrics measured in seconds, since fewer seconds of overlap or silence should mean a higher 1–5 rating. For sighted raters, the two programmatic timing metrics are the strongest predictors: Audio Overlaps (G7) tracks ratings of audio issues and Avg. Silence (G8) tracks ratings of quiet gaps (both p < 0.01 p<0.01 ). VideoA11y-Ref Clear and Descriptive also correlate significantly with the matching ratings. For BLV listeners, No Redundancy (G1.2) and VideoA11y-Ref Clear are significant predictors. Audio Overlaps correlates only weakly with BLV ratings of audio quality, by design of the study: our video player cut off any AD segment as soon as speech began. BLV listeners therefore never heard AD collide with speech; AD that was too long instead showed up as abrupt cutoffs, which listeners penalized under Clarity.

E. 中的全部结果). 对于视力检测器,每个数据点都是带有其AD的额定视频. 对于BLV的听众来说,每个数据点是一个参与者对AutoAD版本的视频(n = 28n = 28)的评分,与该AD的度量分对齐. 以秒计的衡量标准预期是负的,因为减少重叠或沉默的秒数应意味着更高的1-5分。 对视差测定器来说,两个节目计时度量是最强的预测器:音频重叠(G7)跟踪音频问题的评分,和Avg.Silence(G8)跟踪静态差距的评分(均p < 0.01 p<0.01)。 VideoA11y - Refer Clear and Descriptionive 也与对应的收视率有很大关联. 对于BLV收听者,不重复(G1.2)和视频A11y-Ref Clear是重要的预测器。 音频重叠(Audio Overlaps)与BLV对音频质量的收视率只有微弱的关联,通过研究的设计:我们的视频播放器在演讲开始后立刻切断任何AD段. 因此,BLV听众从未听到过AD与讲话相冲突;AD却作为突然的断线出现太久了,听者根据Clarity受到处罚。

blocks.en: Resolving reference-matching bias with Quality-RF . VideoA11y-Ref Accurate correlates negatively with BLV ratings of accuracy ( ρ = − 0.264 \rho=-0.264 ). Two factors explain this. First, listeners without visual access judge accuracy by whether the narration is plausible and consistent [ 10 ] . Second, the reference-based score penalizes correct details that the human describer omitted. Scoring against the video and transcript with Quality-RF eliminates this penalty, flipping Accuracy positive ( ρ = + 0.244 \rho=+0.244 ) and substantially strengthens agreement on Descriptive ( ρ = + 0.583 \rho=+0.583 , p = 0.001 p=0.001 ) and Clear ( ρ = + 0.415 \rho=+0.415 , p = 0.028 p=0.028 ). Together, the guideline metrics and Quality-RF form a fully reference-free evaluation suite that is validated against human judgments and works on unseen videos.
blocks.zh: 解决与质量-RF的参照比对偏差. VideoA11y-Ref 准确度与BLV的准确度评级负相关( ^ = - 0.264\rho=-0.264)。 这有两个原因。 首先,没有目视访问的听众通过叙述是否合理和一致来判断准确性。 其次,基于参考的分数会惩罚人类描述者省略的正确细节. 与视频和录音记录对照使用质素-RF消除了这一处罚,翻转精度正数(^ = + 0.244\rho 0.244),并大大加强了对描述性(^ + 0.583\rho 0.583,p = 0.001 p = 0.001)和Clear(^ + 0.415\rho 0.415,p = 0.028 p = 0.028)的一致,共同构成一个完全无参考性的评价套件,对照人类的判断加以验证,并在无形视频上工作。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion and Broader Impact
blocks.zh: 6. 结论和更广泛的影响

blocks.en: While frontier MLLMs approach human AD in visual descriptiveness, there’s still a clear gap in temporal precision, remaining silence, and narrative pacing for inline AD. Through the MTG-AD dataset with 36 hours of high-quality ground truth, co-created by teams of blind and sighted professionals, and MTG-AD-Eval, an end-to-end reference-free evaluation suite, we demonstrate: • Evaluation-Guided Prompting for Precision: The framework allows development of prompts and harnesses for improved audio description generation. We find that incorporating ASR transcripts and temporal reasoning (via the Gd. + Timing ASR strategy) is essential for balancing content richness with strict temporal constraints, reducing audio overlaps. • Model Performance Benchmarking: Newer-generation omni-modal models (Gemini-3.5 Flash, Qwen-3.5-Omni) raise content prioritization from 0.76 0.76 to 0.79 0.79 – 0.94 0.94 , and Gemini-3.5 Flash cuts speech overlaps to 0.26 0.26 s. Still, no model leads on every metric: the models trade overlap against coverage of the silences, and human AD remains better paced. • User Utility and Reference-Free Evaluation: Our study with blind and low-vision (BLV) participants confirms that while human-crafted AD remains the gold standard for narrative flow, MLLM-generated AD is already highly beneficial for comprehension, and MTG-AD-Eval, our validated reference-free metric suite MTG-AD-Eval ( G1.1–G1.3, G2, G7, G8 and Quality-RF ) correlates substantially with both sighted and BLV human judgments.
blocks.zh: 虽然边疆的MLLMs在视觉描述方面接近人类AD,但是在时间精确度、静默度和内含AD的叙事速度方面仍存在明显的差距。 通过由盲人和有远见的专业人员团队共同制作的具有36小时高质量地面真相的MTG-AD数据集,以及MTG-AD-Eval,一个端到端无参考评价套件,我们展示了: 评估-指导精确性: 该框架允许开发用于改进音频描述生成的提示和利用。 我们认为,纳入ASR记录和时间推理(通过Gd.+Timing ASR战略)对于平衡内容丰富性和严格的时间限制,减少音频重叠至关重要。 • 示范性能 基准:新一代的全方位模型(Gemini-3.5 Flash, Quen-3.5-Omni)将内容优先次序从0.76 0.76提高到0.79 0.79 — 0.94 0.94 和双子座3.5 闪光剪切语重复到0.26 0.26 s. 仍然没有任何模型领先于每个度量:模型贸易与沉默的覆盖重叠,人类反倾销的步伐仍然较好. • 用户效用和无参考评价: 我们与盲目和低视(BLV)参与者进行的研究证实,虽然人造AD仍然是叙述流的金本位标准,但MLLM生成的AD已经非常有利于理解,而MTG-AD-Eval,我们经过验证的无参考的MTG-AD-Eval(G1.1-G1.3,G2,G7,G8和Quality-RF)则与人视和BLV的判断有着实质性的关联.

blocks.en: Guidance for System Designers. Inline AD is a multi-objective constrained problem, and a single aggregate score hides failure modes ( e.g. , high Prioritization with heavy overlaps). For model selection we recommend two stages: (1) Temporal Feasibility Filtering , a hard threshold on Audio Overlaps (G7) so AD does not mask dialogue, and Audio Coverage (G8) ≤ 1 \leq 1 to rule out over-generation (this still leaves some gaps undescribed, as Avg. Silence shows); then (2) Content & Narrative Optimization , maximizing Prioritization (G1.1) , No Redundancy (G1.2) , and Reference-Free Clarity/Descriptiveness ( Quality-RF ) among temporally feasible candidates.
blocks.zh: 系统设计师指南. 内置AD是一个多目标受限的问题,单总分隐藏失败模式(例如高优先级和重重叠). 就模型选择而言,我们建议分两个阶段:(1) 时间可行性过滤,音频重叠(G7)的硬门槛,因此AD不会掩盖对话,以及音频覆盖(G8)\\1\leq 1,排除过多生成(这仍然留下一些空白,如Avg. Silence所示);然后(2) 内容和叙述优化,最大限度地确定优先顺序(G1.1),不重复(G1.2),以及时间上可行的候选人的参考自由清晰度/描述性(质量-RF)。

blocks.en: Limitations. Our automated metrics cover six guidelines from our BLV pilot ( G1.1–G1.3, G2, G7, G8 ), leaving others such as active voice ( G5 ) and prosody ( G10 ) to future work; G1.1 and G2 also depend on MLLM-extracted events ( 𝒟 \mathcal{D} ) and judge calibration, which can under-credit subtle human-observed details. Second, our BLV study ( 7 7 participants, 28 28 full-length video evaluations) gives rich paired comparisons, but larger cohorts across more genres would better capture individual preferences. Finally, our temporal metrics render AD with a standard TTS engine at a fixed 1.2 × 1.2\times speaking rate, and absolute overlap and coverage values depend on this rate. We leave the speaking rate to future work; faster or adaptive per-gap speech could fit richer descriptions into the silences.
blocks.zh: 限制。 我们的自动化度量衡涵盖我们的BLV飞行员(G1.1–G1.3,G2,G7,G8)的六条准则,其他如主动语音(G5)和prosody(G10)则留待未来工作;G1.1和G2还依赖于MLLLM提取的事件(D\mathcal{D})和判断校准,这些校准可以低估人类观察的微妙细节. 第二,我们的BLV研究(7,7名参与者,28名全长视频评价)提供了丰富的配对比较,但跨更多流派的较大组群将更好地捕捉个人喜好. 最后,我们的时间度量衡使AD与标准TTS引擎以固定的1.2×1.2\时的语音率制成,绝对重叠值和覆盖值取决于这个率. 我们把发言率留给未来工作;更快或适应性强的每段发言可以将更丰富的描述融入沉默。

blocks.en: Dataset and Code Release. We release MTG-AD under CC-BY-4.0 ( hf.co/datasets/google/mind-the-gap-inline-ad ) and MTG-AD-Eval under Apache-2.0 ( github.com/google/mtg-ad ). Bundling human and model ADs, ASR transcripts, and pre-extracted visual events ( 𝒟 \mathcal{D} ) to support reproducibility, re-use and further development of the evaluation frameworks.
blocks.zh: 数据集和代码发布. 在CC-BY-4.0(hf.co/datasets/google/mind-the-gap-inline-ad)和Apache-2.0(github.com/google/mtg-ad)下发布MTG-AD-Eval. 捆绑人与型号AD,ASR笔录,以及预摘录的视觉事件(D\mathcal{D}),支持可复制,再使用和进一步发展评价框架.

blocks.en: Broader Impact. The MTG-AD dataset and MTG-AD-Eval reference-free evaluation framework can support automated auditing and generation of inline AD for user-generated tutorials, educational content, and vlogs at scale, and could serve as video accessibility indicators for BLV audiences. It also carries risks: generated AD can hallucinate details that mislead BLV users or misrepresent the creator’s intent, which listeners cannot easily verify, so AI-generated AD should be labeled as such.
blocks.zh: 更宽的影响。 MTG-AD数据集和MTG-AD-Eval无参考评价框架可以支持自动审计和生成内部AD,用于用户生成的辅导,教育内容,以及规模的Vlog,并且可以作为BLV受众的视频访问指标. 也带有风险:生成的AD可以产生误导BLV用户或歪曲创作者意图的幻觉,而听者无法轻易验证,所以AI生成的AD应该被贴上这样的标签.

blocks.en: For the analysis of the main experiments in this work, we use a subset of our guidelines that we prioritized for evaluation based on a pilot study with BLV audience members reviewing descriptions created with a basic prompt ( e.g. , “Create an audio description”). In the pilot study BLV users surfaced issues that most negatively impacted their experience, and these issues informed our choice of guidelines for initial metrics ( G1.1-1.3 , G2 , G7 , G8 ).

blocks.en: D.1 BLV Qualitative Feedback and Individual Preference Variance
blocks.zh: D.1 BLV 定性反馈和个人优惠差异

blocks.en: Consistent with prior accessibility literature [ 20 , 17 , 11 ] , post-task interviews with our 7 BLV participants ( 28 28 paired video evaluations) revealed substantial individual-level and genre-dependent variance in AD preferences. While professional human AD was favored overall ( 53.6 % 53.6\% ) for its smooth narrative flow, concise phrasing, and natural integration around dialogue pauses, AutoAD ( Gemini-2.5 Flash with Gd. + Timing ASR ) was preferred in 46.4 % 46.4\% of comparisons—particularly on visually dense travel, nature, and instructional videos where participants valued exhaustive enumeration of visual objects, settings, and on-screen text. Conversely, when AutoAD was penalized, participants cited occasional redundancy with sound effects or abrupt sentence truncation when an AD segment reached the onset of video speech.
blocks.zh: 根据先前的无障碍文献[20、17、11],与我们7名BLV参与者进行的任务后访谈(28名28对视频评价)表明,在AD偏好方面,个人层面和不同寻常的差异很大。 虽然专业的人类AD因其平稳的叙事流程、简洁的词句和围绕对话暂停的自然融合而总体上得到青睐(53.6%-53.6%),但AutoAD(双子2.5闪光与Gd.+Timing ASR)在46.4%的比较中得到青睐——特别是在视觉稠密的旅行、自然和教学视频方面,参与者重视详尽列举视觉物体、设置和屏幕文本。 反之,当AutoAD受到处罚时,与会者则提到,当AutoAD部分进入视频讲话时,偶尔会出现有声音效果的冗余或突然的句子短音。

blocks.en: Ablation of Reference-Free Input Representations. We evaluated four reference-free input configurations for Quality-RF : (1) video-only , (2) video + ASR transcript , (3) dense visual info + ASR , and (4) video + dense visual info + ASR . We found that providing the raw video + ASR transcript ( Tab. 10 , Fig. 26 ) achieves the strongest overall correlation across all four dimensions ( ρ = + 0.583 \rho=+0.583 on Descriptive, ρ = + 0.415 \rho=+0.415 on Clear, and ρ = + 0.244 \rho=+0.244 on Accurate), whereas text-only dense visual info + ASR achieves the highest standalone Accuracy correlation ( ρ = + 0.289 \rho=+0.289 ) when raw video frames cannot be passed to the judge.

blocks.en: TTS Speaking Rate. Our temporal metrics ( G7 , G8 ) render AD segments with an off-the-shelf TTS engine at a fixed 1.2 × 1.2\times speaking rate. Because a segment’s spoken duration scales inversely with the rate, faster speech shortens AD intervals and reduces overlap seconds, and slower speech lengthens them; the absolute values of these metrics therefore depend on the chosen rate. We do not study other rates here. Faster or adaptive per-gap speaking rates are a promising direction, as they would allow more descriptions to fit into the available silences.
blocks.zh: TTS话速率. 我们的时间度量衡(G7,G8)使AD片段具有现成的TTS引擎,使用固定的1.2×1.2的发声率. 由于某一段的口语持续时间与速率相反,因此更快的口语缩短了AD间隔并减少了重叠秒,而较慢的口语延长了它们;因此,这些度量的绝对值取决于选择的速率. 我们在这里不研究其他费率。 更快或适应性强的每个差距的演讲率是一个很有希望的方向,因为它们将允许更多的描述适应现有的沉默。

大多数信息都是相关的。 □ 绝对同意。 所有信息都是相关的。 4. 一致性/重复性: 对信息用户的描述已经来自视频的音频和先前的描述. □ 强烈不同意。 所有描述都重复了用户从视频的音频或先前描述中已经知道的信息. {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}请说 {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}我还是有点意见不一 大多数描述都重复了用户从视频音频或先前描述中已经知道的信息. □ 要么同意要么不同意。 有些说明提供了新的信息,但有些则包括用户从音频或先前的说明中已经知道的信息。 □ 平面略为同意。 大多数描述提供了新的信息,但有些描述包括用户从视频音频或先前描述中已经知道的信息。 □ 绝对同意。 所有描述都提供了新的信息,补充了现有视频的音频和先前的描述。 5. 总体质量:总体来说,描述的内容是高质量的,在没有视觉的情况下参与倾听。 □ 强烈不同意。 叙述的所有内容都具有重大的质量问题,难以跟踪或不倾听。 例如,描述过于重复和乏味,或者对字符、对象或设置的引用不一致,使其难以遵循。 {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}请说 {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}我还是有点意见不一 叙述的大部分内容都有重大的质量问题,难以跟踪或不倾听。 □ 要么同意要么不同意。 叙述中的一些内容容易跟踪,也容易参与倾听。 有些时候存在质量问题,使叙述难以跟踪或不倾听。 □ 平面略为同意。 叙述中的大部分内容都容易跟踪并参与倾听. 叙述的语言大多是清晰的、说明性的和积极的。 □ 绝对同意。 叙述中的所有内容都易于跟踪和倾听。 叙述中的语言是完全清楚的、说明性的和积极的。 6. 明确性:仅考虑到音频,描述清楚,易于跟踪。 □ 强烈不同意。 在单独考虑音频中的信息时,所有描述都不清楚或难以遵循(例如,对字符、设置或对象使用不明确或不一致的引用)。 {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}请说 {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}我还是有点意见不一 大多数描述都不清楚或难以遵循,但在仅考虑音频中的信息时,有些描述很容易遵循. □ 要么同意要么不同意。 有些描述是清楚的,容易遵循,有些在仅考虑音频中的信息时并不明确或难以遵循. {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}你同意吗? 大部分描述包括生动的细节,描述大多保持简洁的叙事流程. □ 绝对同意。 所有描述都包含生动的细节,同时保持简洁的叙事流程. 8. 目标: 这些描述是客观的,因为它们报告可见的东西而不增加个人意见或假设(例如关于人物关系或身份属性)。 □ 强烈不同意。 所有描述都包含主观观点或假设. {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}请说 {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}我还是有点意见不一 大多数描述包括主观观点或假设. □ 要么同意要么不同意。 有些描述是客观的,但有些描述包括主观意见或假设。 {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}你同意吗? 大多数描述是清楚的,没有音频问题。 □ 绝对同意。 所有描述都是清晰的,没有音频问题。 11. 沉默的差距: 在描述中不存在很大的沉默空白(6-10s的沉默空白). □ 强烈不同意。 视频中的所有沉默空白都没有描述. {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}请说 {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}我还是有点意见不一 整个录像中经常出现长时间的沉默空白。 □ 要么同意要么不同意。 整个视频中存在一些长时间的沉默空白. □ 平面略为同意。 视频中存在一两次长时间的沉默空白. □ 绝对同意。 沉默没有长期的差距。

blocks.zh: 强烈不同意. 叙述的所有内容都具有重大的质量问题,难以跟踪或不倾听。 例如,描述过于重复和乏味,或者对字符、对象或设置的引用不一致,使其难以遵循。

blocks.en: The output format must be exactly like this:
blocks.zh: 输出格式必须是这样的:

blocks.en: * One scene description per line. * Each description follows the format <timestamp> <description> • * The timestamp must be in the format 00:00:00.000 (hh:mm:ss.ms) followed by a "-". * The descriptions must be sorted by timestamp in ascending order. * **CRUCIAL**: The descriptions must follow this format and cover the entire video.
blocks.zh: * 《大会正式记录,第五十八届会议,补编第5号》(A/C.6/61/Rev.1)。 每行一个场景描述. * 每种说明都遵循 " 时间戳 " 和 " 描述 " 的格式。 * 时间戳必须采用00:00:00.000(hh:mm:s.ms)的格式,然后是"-". * 描述必须按照递增顺序按时间戳排序. * ** CRUCIAL**:说明必须遵循这一格式,并覆盖整个视频。

Guideline AD Prompt You are an expert audio description writer. Your task is to write high-quality audio descriptions for videos,
ensuring accessibility for visually impaired viewers.
Audio descriptions should narrate key visual elements
that are not already conveyed through the dialogue or other audio elements. Please adhere to the following guidelines: What to Describe: * Describe what you see. Focus on the essential visual information needed to understand the scene. * Be concise. * Always read on-screen text exactly as it appears. * Be factual, objective, and avoid speculation. * Use proper terminology and names whenever possible. * All of the descriptions will need to fit in the space between dialog
(assume 1-3 words per second when spoken aloud).
If there is no space, then you need to skip the description. * Try to match the mood of the video with your descriptions. * Describe color only when it is vital to the comprehension of content. ** CRUCIAL: ** Your descriptions must cover the entire video. What NOT to Describe: * Do not talk over the dialog or any other essential audio. * Do not describe what can be inferred from the audio. * Do not over-describe; less is more. Keep descriptions brief and to the point. * Do not interpret or editorialize. Stick to describing what is visually present. * Do not give away secrets, surprises, or sight gags before they happen. * Do not censor (sex, violence, gore, emotions), describe them accurately. * Do not describe obvious sound cues such as dialogue, a phone ringing, or a dog barking. Remember to only place descriptions between gaps of speech.
Strive for clear, concise, and informative audio descriptions
that enhance the viewing experience without distracting from the original content. The output format must be a valid JSON with a single field called "response" containing the following: * One scene description per line. * Each description follows the format <timestamp>-STANDARD <description> • * The timestamp must be in seconds in the format 0:00:00.000 (h:mm:ss.ms) followed by a "-" • * The type of description should always be STANDARD • * The description must be in a single line. * The descriptions must be sorted by timestamp in ascending order. * **CRUCIAL**: The descriptions must follow this format and cover the entire video. * **CRUCIAL**: The format must be valid.

VideoA11y Prompt You are an expert evaluator with a deep understanding of video description quality, particularly for making content accessible to blind and low vision (BLV) individuals. Your role is to assess and rate video descriptions based on specific metrics. Task: I have two video descriptions: one is the ground truth, and the other is generated by a model. Additionally, I have four evaluation metrics: Descriptive, Objective, Accurate, and Clear. Please evaluate the model-generated description using the above metrics. Provide a rating from 1 to 5 for each metric, and briefly explain the reasons for each rating. Metrics Definition: 1. Descriptive: A descriptive description should provide vivid details about objects, people, and settings while maintaining a concise narrative flow. It should include essential information about the appearance of individuals, such as their clothing, facial expressions, and actions, and visual properties of objects, such as color and shape. For example, "A smiling woman, wearing a loose white dress, types on a laptop in a softly lit room." 2. Objective: An objective description should report what is visible without adding personal opinions or assumptions. For instance, describe two people as "a woman and a man" without adding any relationship context unless it is mentioned. It should also avoid guessing personal attributes like racial or gender identities unless explicitly clear. 3. Accurate: An accurate description should aim for precision in describing visible elements without imagination. It should ensure that all details, such as colors and spatial arrangements, are reported correctly. For instance, "Blue sky with white clouds" instead of "White sky with blue clouds" if that is what appears. Additionally, it should avoid adding unnecessary details that do not contribute to a deeper understanding of the scene. 4. Clear: A clear description should present information in the videos in a way that is easy to follow for blind and low vision individuals. It should describe the object or character’s properties before the actions or relationships with other objects or characters. For example, "A man wearing sunglasses plays the piano." Pronouns should only be used when it is clear who they refer to, and the description should include any on-screen text if it is central to understanding. For instance, "A man in a black polo shirt is speaking. He is in a studio setting with a red couch and a blue background featuring the text ’Talk of the Town’". Input: - Ground truth video description: <ground_truth_desc> GROUND_TRUTH_DESC_GOES_HERE_IF_AVAILABLE </ground_truth_desc> Model-generated video description:
<generated_desc> GENERATED_DESC_GOES_HERE_IF_AVAILABLE </generated_desc> Output Format: Return the result as a string format dictionary with
